content.title: Live updates at the 2026 Final Four in Indianapolis
content.text: Sort By:Oldest FirstLatest10:26 pm, April 4, 2026 Michigan made it look easy in the Final Four, steamrolling Arizona, 91-73. The Wolverines are back in the national championship game for the first time since 2018, when they fell to Villanova. Michigan becomes the first team in NCAA tournament history to score 90+ points in five consecutive games. Michigan came out hot in this one, jumping out to an early 10-1 lead and holding it all the way until the final buzzer, even leading by as many as 30 points in the second half. The Wolverines kept Arizona locked up all night, holding the Wildcats to 37% from the field. Aday Mara led the Wolverines with 26 points and nine rebounds, dominating Arizona in the paint all night. Elliot Cadeau finished with a double-double: 13 points and 10 assists. Aday Mara is having a NIGHT 😤#MarchMadness @umichbball pic.twitter.com/wACprxxAUO — NCAA March Madness (@MarchMadnessMBB) April 5, 2026 Michigan moves on to face UConn in the title game at 8:50 p.m. ET on Monday, April 6. The Wolverines will look to capture their first championship since 1989, when they defeated Seton Hall. 9:55 pm, April 4, 2026It's all Michigan. The Wolverines have now made 7 out of 7 of their last field goals and are on a 6-0 run over a 28-second period. Michigan fans have for sure asserted their dominance in the stadium. MICHIGAN KEEPS POURING IT ON ☔️#MarchMadness @umichbball pic.twitter.com/yiyHA0vLVP — NCAA March Madness (@MarchMadnessMBB) April 5, 2026 9:23 pm, April 4, 2026The Wolverines have been on fire in the first half, making all their free throws and having seven different players score at least five points each. MOREZ JOHNSON OMG 😱 pic.twitter.com/dwD9PdTLq1 — NCAA March Madness (@MarchMadnessMBB) April 5, 2026 One major storyline that we are following is that Yaxel Lendeborg has played only five minutes, during which he picked up two early fouls and had to leave the court due to an injury. Meanwhile, Arizona is struggling to find its rhythm, shooting 12 for 32 from the field. Jaden Bradley has now picked up his third foul, and Arizona cannot afford to have him on the bench right now, as they are currently down by 16 points. 8:58 pm, April 4, 2026 Michigan has established a strong lead over Arizona, but the Wildcats have now gone on an 11-2 run, cutting the Wolverines' lead to seven points with 6:56 remaining. The atmosphere in the arena is electric, as fans from both sides are fully engaged, watching closely to see if Arizona can continue this momentum and mount a potential comeback. Meanwhile, Michigan is feeling the pressure and must buckle down to maintain its advantage and secure the win as the final minutes of the first half approach. 8:04 pm, April 4, 2026 It's a clash of juggernauts as Arizona and Michigan fight for a date with the Huskies in the title game. Tip time is set for 9:19 p.m. ET on TBS. 7:43 pm, April 4, 2026 — Jalen Rose (@JalenRose) April 4, 2026 A legendary reunion is happening tonight, and you won’t want to miss it. Michigan’s iconic “Fab Five” are back together for a special alternate broadcast of the Michigan–Arizona Final Four matchup. Chris Webber, Jalen Rose, Juwan Howard, Jimmy King and Ray Jackson changed college basketball forever, leading Michigan to back-to-back national title games in 1992 and 1993 as the first team to start five freshmen. Now they’re watching it all unfold live, sharing real-time reactions, stories and insight throughout the game. 📺 Watch the Fab Five AltCast on truTV and HBO Max 7:21 pm, April 4, 2026 No. 2 UConn took a 14-point lead and held off No. 3 Illinois, 71-62, to advance to the national championship game. The Huskies return to the title game in search of their third championship in four years. UConn nearly led this game wire-to-wire — Illinois briefly led in the first half 22-21 before the Huskies reclaimed the lead and never gave it up. UConn’s stifling defense limited Illinois’ ball movement, holding the Illini to just three total assists and forcing eight turnovers. Meanwhile, the Huskies spread the ball around well, racking up 14 team assists as three starters put up double-digit points. Tarris Reed Jr. led UConn with 17 points and 11 rebounds. Illinois went on an 10-0 run to close the gap late in the second half, cutting the UConn lead to four with 6:08 to play, but the Huskies locked it down and pulled away, and Braylon Mullins delivered a dagger 3-pointer to secure their spot in the championship game. Mr. Basketball doing Mr. Basketball things back in Indy pic.twitter.com/CLWZyEpSi7 — UConn Men's Basketball (@UConnMBB) April 5, 2026 UConn will face the winner of No. 1 Arizona and No. 1 Michigan as the Huskies chase their third title in four seasons, which would mark the best stretch since UCLA won 10 titles in 12 years from 1964-75. 7:04 pm, April 4, 2026The Illini crowd is fired up in Lucas Oil, as they are just within 5. Illinois went on a 10-0 run over 4:33, while UConn faced a 5-minute scoring drought. Illinois is shooting only 33 percent to UConn's 36, but the Illini have made 17 free throws to the Huskies' eight. We'll see if the Illini can make the complete comeback. It would tie for the fifth-largest comeback win in Final Four history. 6:38 pm, April 4, 2026The Fighting Illini are desperately trying to get back into the game. After facing their largest deficit of the season, they have now closed the gap to within eight points. Meanwhile, Braylon Mullins and Tarris Reed, who led the Huskies in the first half, have not scored any points in the second half. 6:06 pm, April 4, 2026Illinois briefly grabbed its first lead of the night after finding a defensive rhythm, but UConn answered quickly and regained control behind an efficient stretch from Tarris Reed Jr and Braylon Mullins, who are powering the Huskies offensively so far. Reed is 5 of 8 from the field, while Mullins leads all scorers with 12 points. UConn also has nine assists without any turnovers, while the Illinis had just one assist in the first half. Braylon Mullins AGAIN 👌#MarchMadness @UConnMBB pic.twitter.com/H9ZLt7MuPv — NCAA March Madness (@MarchMadnessMBB) April 4, 2026 Tarris Reed going for 3️⃣ the hard way 💪#MarchMadness @UConnMBB pic.twitter.com/YIGVUZ5Xra — NCAA March Madness (@MarchMadnessMBB) April 4, 2026 5:28 pm, April 4, 2026The first semifinal game is underway, with UConn leading by six as we figure out the first half of the national championship matchup now. Braylon Mullins was the last scorer in the Elite Eight and picked up right where he left off, scoring the Huskies' first points. — NCAA March Madness (@MarchMadnessMBB) April 4, 2026 3:56 pm, April 4, 2026 We’ve made it inside Lucas Oil Stadium. Fans battled through a quick downpour right at the time gates opened, but the energy hasn’t dipped — it’s only building as we get closer to tip. UConn and Illinois tip off at 6:09 p.m. ET, and we’ve got you covered with everything from live game updates to behind-the-scenes moments all night long. We’re posted up right behind the UConn student section, but Illinois fans are making their presence known early. As the Huskies stepped onto the court for warmups, boos immediately rang out across the stadium — a clear sign this crowd is leaning Illini. With Champaign just about 120 miles away, Illinois fans are showing up in full force and turning this into a near-home environment. The seats are filling, the noise is rising and soon we will have a heavyweight showdown unfold. Follow along here for live updates, highlights and everything you might miss in the moment. 3:13 pm, April 4, 2026 We started tracking around 36 million brackets during March Madness across the major online games. All perfect brackets busted in the second round when No. 6 Tennessee defeated No. 3 Virginia on Game No. 44 of March Madness. But our bracket tracking continued even after the chase for perfection ended. With the Final Four set in Indianapolis, we discovered that only a small percentage of brackets went 4 for 4 in picking the national semifinalists. In fact, only 12,624 brackets in the Men's Bracket Challenge Game correctly picked Arizona, Michigan, UConn and Illinois to reach the Final Four. Here’s how those brackets stack up when it comes to picking a national champion: Arizona: 37.99% Michigan: 29.97% UConn: 20.21% Illinois: 11.83% Arizona leads the way as the most-picked champion, with Michigan close behind. Just 11.83% — 1,493 brackets — picked Illinois. Now we’ll see who got it right. 1:21 pm, April 4, 2026As we made our way around Lucas Oil Stadium, talking with fans, we accidentally ran into a special group: Braylon Mullins’ family. — NCAA March Madness (@MarchMadnessMBB) April 3, 2026 Just days after his iconic game-winner sent UConn past Duke and into the Final Four, Mullins' family shared what it was like watching that moment unfold in real time, from where they were sitting to the emotions that followed. It’s a memory they won’t forget. Now, Mullins returns to his hometown with a chance to compete for a national title — and his family will be right there watching it all again. 8:02 am, April 4, 2026Good morning from Indianapolis. Today, we find out who's moving on to the national championship. — NCAA March Madness (@MarchMadnessMBB) April 4, 2026 We’re here providing on-site coverage all weekend for this year’s Final Four. No. 1 UConn and Illinois tip things off at 6:09 p.m. ET, followed by Michigan and Arizona at 8:54 p.m. ET — two heavyweight battles with everything on the line. The Huskies are building a modern dynasty and sit two wins away from a third national championship in four years. Illinois is back in the Final Four for the first time since 2005, looking to ride its momentum back to the top. Arizona returns to Indianapolis — the same city where it won it all in 1997 — looking to capture its first national title since that year, while Michigan is back for the first time since 2018, chasing its first championship since 1989 after a dominant run all season.
